stem:
Priya stirs a spoonful of sugar into a glass of water until the sugar disappears completely. She finds that every sip from the glass tastes equally sweet, and no separate layer of sugar can be seen anywhere in the water.

Why is this mixture classified as a solution?

options.text: Because two substances are present together in the glass
Because the sugar was stirred into the water with a spoon
Because sugar and water are both pure substances
Because the sugar is evenly distributed throughout the water

teacher.key_rationale: A mixture is a solution only when its components are evenly distributed and not visible separately; the even distribution (uniform sweetness, no separate layer) is the deciding feature, so D is correct. A traps students who call any two-substance mixture a solution; B and C are irrelevant conditions.
